title: The Widest Ramp

concept.title: Only the prefix minimums can be the start of the best ramp
body: A **ramp** is a pair of indexes `i < j` with `a[i] <= a[j]`. Its width is `j - i`. We want the widest ramp. A candidate for the **left** end `i` is useful only if it is a new **strict minimum** of the prefix: if some earlier element is `<=` `a[i]`, then using that earlier element is at least as good (it is further to the left and also not larger). So collect these candidates in a stack: the indexes of the strictly decreasing prefix minimums.

Now look for the right end `j` **from the right to the left**. For each `j`, as long as the top candidate has `a[top] <= a[j]`, the pair is a ramp: record the width `j - top` and **pop** the candidate. Why can we pop it? Any later right end (further to the left) is closer to the candidate, so the width would only be smaller; the candidate cannot give a better answer. The candidates with smaller indexes are lower in the stack and the stack decreases in value, so the pop order is right.
Each index is pushed once and popped at most once: O(n).

statement: A ramp in an array is a pair of positions `i < j` with `a[i] <= a[j]`; its width is `j - i`. Print the largest width of a ramp, or 0 if there is no ramp.
hints: The left end of the best ramp is always a strict prefix minimum.
Collect the prefix minimums on a stack (as indexes).
Scan the right end from the right and pop every candidate that forms a ramp with it.
